This revision petition is filed by the petitioners being
aggrieved by the concurrent findings of the Courts below.

The
petitioners have been directed to provide necessary amenities
to the respondent to reside comfortably in her portion of the
shared household.

In addition to that the petitioners have been
directed to pay a sum of Rs.3,000/- to the respondent as
maintenance and also directed to pay rent not exceeding Rs.
3,000/- per month and also directed to pay compensation of

2. Brief facts of the case are as under:

The respondent namely Smt. Bharathi is the wife of
Sridhar.

She had filed Criminal Miscellaneous Petition before
the Trial Court seeking maintenance against the petitioners
herein.

The facts urged in this petition unfolded in such a way
that her father-in-law had three wives.

Krishnamurthy and
Ganesh are the children born to the first wife.

Narasimha,
Subbaraya and Sridhar are the children of the second wife.

Her
father-in-law after the death of the second wife, married third

wife-Gowramma.
She had a child namely Raghavendra.

The
petitioner No.5 is the wife of petitioner No.2-Narasimha.

3. The respondent-Smt.Bharathi married Sridhar on
07.09.2003 at Jannapura, Bhadravathi as per Hindu customs.

Her husband was suffering from alcoholic syndrome and also he
was suffering from paralysis.

The respondent herein was
residing along with the petitioners herein in her matrimonial
house.

At the time of marriage, it was told her that the
property of her father-in-law has been divided among the
brothers. However, it was not divided even after her marriage
and the share of her husband was not allotted.
 4.

In the month of March-2011, when the petitioner

have assaulted her husband and caused injuries.

Immediately,
she went to her matrimonial home and she admitted her
husband to the Manipal Hospital.

The said Sridhar took
treatment for one month.

After obtaining treatment from the
said hospital, she went to her matrimonial home along with her
husband.
However, she was also beaten by her brother-in-laws.
She lodged a complaint against her brother-in-laws.

The
respondent-Smt.Bharathi lodged a complaint at different Forum
for seeking justice and also compensation from her brother-in-

In the meantime, her husband and other family members
had entered into compromise and got executed Ex.P6-
Memorandum of understanding.

As per the said settlement, the
petitioners herein had agreed to pay of Rs.1,20,000/- per year
as the share of her husband.

5. As per the said agreement, the petitioners herein
had to pay advance of Rs.50,000/- towards rent for her
separate residence.
However, the said amount was not given.

As the petitioners herein failed to discharge their obligations,
the respondent approached the Trial Court under the Protection
of Women from Domestic Violence (for short, 'Pwdv') Act,
2005.

The Trial Court after appreciating both the oral and
documentary evidence on record passed an order as stated
supra.
Even in the appeal, it has been confirmed.

petitioners that the petitioners herein are admittedly the family

herein.

The respondent herein after her marriage was not
staying with the petitioners at any point of time.

Both the

2003.

In the year 2011, the brother of petitioner No.2 got
admitted to the Manipal Hospital and the petitioners got him
treated by spending money.
 7.

It is further submitted that the husband of the
respondent had 1 acre 10 guntas of arecanut plantation and
yield of the said garden has been taken by the said Sridhar
himself.

On 07.04.2010, the agreement was executed between
the petitioners herein and the respondent.

As per the said
agreement, the amount was being paid regularly, however, the
respondent herein filed a false case only in order to give trouble
in one or the other pretext.

However, the Trial Court failed to
consider the defence of the petitioners herein and passed an
order to pay the maintenance which is not proper and
therefore, the same is liable to be set aside.

Making such

11 . After having heard the learned counsel for the
respective parties and also perused the findings of the Courts
below, it is relevant to make out points are as under:
 a) Whether the petitioners made out a ground to
 interfere with the findings of the Trial Court?
 b) Whether the respondent proved the case to
 get maintenance from the petitioners herein?

My answer to the above points are as under:
 Point No.1: Partly allowed;
 Point No.2: Affirmative.
 12.

It is an admitted fact that petitioners No.2 and 3
are the own brothers of the husband of the respondent.
Petitioner No.4 is the step brother of her husband.

Smt. 
Gowramma is the mother-in-law of the respondent.

Petitioner
No.5 is the co-sister of the respondent.

In order to get an order
for maintenance from the brothers of her husband, it is
Smt Gowramma vs Smt Bharathi on 15 July, 2024
Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/140822092/
7

necessary to prove that she had shared house hold of the joint
 -9-
 Crl.Rp No. 1099 of 2021
family and the status of the joint family still in existence
without making any partition.

13 . In this context, now it is relevant to refer the
judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Ajay Kumar
Vs. Latha @ Shruthi and Others5.
Paragraph number-14 of
the said judgment

reads thus:
 "14.

At the present stage, there are sufficient
 averments in the complaint to sustain the order for the
 award of interim maintenance.

Paragraph 10 of the
 complaint prima facie indicates that the case of the
 complainants is that the house where the first
 respondent and her spouse resided, belong to a joint
 family.

The appellant and his brother (who was the
 spouse of the first respondent and father of the second
 respondent) carried on a joint business.

The appellant
 resided in the same household.

Ultimately, whether the
 requirements of Section 2(f); Section 2(q); and Section
 2(s) are fulfilled is a matter of evidence which will be
 adjudicated upon at the trial.

At this stage, for the
 purpose of an interim order for maintenance, there was
 material which justifies the issuance of a direction in
 regard to the payment of maintenance."
 14.

On careful reading of the dictum of the Hon'ble
Supreme Court which indicates that to get an order of
maintenance and compensation from other male members of
5
 (2019) 15 Scc 352
 - 10 -
 Crl.Rp No. 1099 of 2021
the joint family, the respondent has to prove that the petitioner
herself resided together in the house which belongs to the joint
family.
Smt Gowramma vs Smt Bharathi on 15 July, 2024

Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/140822092/
8

 15.

After considering the dictum of the Hon'ble
Supreme Court, now it is necessary to refer the following
definitions for the purpose of clarification.

"2(f) -domestic relationship" means a relationship
 between two persons who live or have, at any point of
 time, lived together in a shared household, when they are
 related by consanguinity, marriage or through a
 relationship in the nature of marriage, adoption or are
 family members living together as a joint family,"
 The expression "shared household" is defined in
Section 2(s) as follows:
 "2. (s) "shared household" means a household
 where the person aggrieved lives or at any stage has lived
 in a domestic relationship either singly or along with the
 respondent includes such a household whether owned or
 tenanted either jointly by the aggrieved person and the
 respondent, or owned or tenanted by either of them in
 respect of which either the aggrieved person or the
 respondent or both joint or singly have any right, title,
 interest or equity and includes such a household which
 may belong to the joint family of which the respondent is
 a member, irrespective of whether the respondent or the
 aggrieved person has any right, title or interest in the
 shared household."
 - 11 -
 Crl.Rp No. 1099 of 2021
 "2. (q) "respondent" means any adult male person
 who is, or has been, in a domestic relationship with the
 aggrieved person and against whom the aggrieved person
 has sought any relief under this Act:
 Provided that an aggrieved wife or female living in a
 relationship in the nature of a marriage may also file a
 complaint against a relative of the husband or the male
 partner."
 16.

On careful reading of the definition as stipulated by
the Act, it can be inferred that the aggrieved woman under the
Act can also file a claim seeking for similar relief as that of
claim against her husband, to the other male member of the
Smt Gowramma vs Smt Bharathi on 15 July, 2024
Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/140822092/
9

joint family.

However, the Act excluded the women from being
claimed the relief by the aggrieved woman.

Therefore, the
Courts below have failed to take note of the definition properly
and directed all the petitioners to pay compensation and
maintenance to the respondent herein which needs to be
interfered.

In such a way, the order passed by the Courts below
against the women who are the petitioner Nos. 1 and 5 are
unsustainable.

17. In the present case, the respondent herein proved
that she is a married woman.

Her marriage had been
solemnized with Sridhar who is the brother of petitioner Nos. 2
to 4.

The said Sridhar addicted to the alcohol and was also
 - 12 -
 Crl.Rp No. 1099 of 2021
suffering from paralysis.

The joint family properties though
stated to have been divided between the brothers, it was being
looked after by the petitioner Nos.2 to 4.

To substantiate the
contention of the respondent, it is necessary to consider Ex.P6.

The said document is construed as memorandum of
understanding between the family members and the same has
been admitted by R.W.1.

Though some of the documents
showed that the husband of the respondent got mutated his
share in the revenue records, as per the evidence of P.W.1, the
documents have been changed only for the purpose of securing
the loan from the agricultural bank at the instance of petitioner
Nos. 2 to 4.

Smt Gowramma vs Smt Bharathi on 15 July, 2024
Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/140822092/
10

 18.
P.W.1 further deposed in her evidence that she was

staying along with the petitioners in the joint family properties
by preparing separate food, however, living in the same
shelter
. The same has also been admitted by R.W.1.

It is also
stated in the evidence of R.W.1 that he had paid Rs.1,20,000/-
for the year 2010.

Thereafter, he stopped making payment as
per Ex.P.6-MOU.

The respondent neither obtained the property
as a share of her husband nor getting any monetary benefits as
per Ex.P6-MOU.

In such a way, it can be stated that the
respondent had proved her case that herself and her husband
 - 13 -
 Crl.Rp No. 1099 of 2021
are still living under the joint family status and hence, she is
entitled for maintenance and compensation as per the Act.
 19.

In the meantime, the learned counsel for the
petitioners raised the legal point that the alleged domestic
violence stated to have taken place in the year 2010.

However,
the petition is filed by the respondent in the year 2012 which is
hopelessly barred and the said miscellaneous complaint ought
not to have been considered by the Trial Court.

The said
question is concerned, it is relevant to refer the provision under
Section 31 of the P.W.D.V., Act which reads thus:
 "31. Penalty for breach of protection order by the
 respondent:-
 (1) A breach of protection order or of an interim
 protection order, by the respondent shall be an
 offence under this Act and shall be punishable with
 imprisonment of either description for a term
 which may extend to one year or with fine which
Smt Gowramma vs Smt Bharathi on 15 July, 2024
Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/140822092/
11

 may extend to twenty thousand rupees or with
 both.
 (2) The offence under sub-section (1) shall as far as
 practicable be tried by the Magistrate who had
 passed the order, the breach of which has been
 alleged to have been caused by the accused.

(3) While framing charges under sub-section (1), the
 Magistrate may also frame charges under section
 498A of the Indian Penal Code (45 of 1860) or any
 other provision of that Code or the Dowry
 Prohibition Act, 1961 (28 of 1961), as the case
 may be, if the facts disclose the commission of an
 offence under those provisions."
 - 14 -
 Crl.Rp No. 1099 of 2021
 20.

On careful reading of the above said provision, it
makes it clear that the limitation to take cognizance would not
arise as it is a Special Act and it is settled principle of law that
Special Act prevails over the General Act.

When the Special Act
did not specify the time limit to take cognizance, it need not be
gone into searching of the general provision. Though Schedule-
Ii of the Code of Criminal Procedure provided certain
classification of offences against other laws, the limitation to
take cognizance has not specified therein.

Therefore, as regards
taking cognizance of the offence under Section of P.W.D.V Act,
Section 468 of Cr.P.C cannot be applicable.

Therefore, the
contention raised by the learned counsel for petitioners in
respect of limitation to take cognizance cannot be sustained.

Accordingly, contention of the learned counsel for petitioners
stands rejected.

21 . In the light of the observations made above, I
answered the points stated supra and I proceed to pass the

a) The Criminal Revision Petition is allowed-in-part.
